style=""><font style="">Articles are normally obtained from the&nbsp;</font><span style="font-family: Consolas, &quot;Courier New&quot;, monospace; white-space: pre;"><font style="">collect_articles()</font></span><span style="background-color: transparent;">&nbsp;tool in the collector MCP server. The&nbsp;</span></font><span style="background-color: transparent; white-space: pre;"><font face="Consolas, Courier New, monospace">get_articles_about</font></span><span style="background-color: transparent; font-family: Consolas, &quot;Courier New&quot;, monospace; white-space: pre;">(topics)</span><span style="background-color: transparent;">&nbsp;tool can be used to get more articles about a topic.</span></font></p><p><font style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"><font style="background-color: transparent;"><span style="background-color: transparent;">the article_id is a string of the form: "%publication_date%-%source_id%-%article_title_hash%" it can be used to uniquely identify the article and acts as the </span></font><span style="background-color: transparent;">retrieval</span><span style="background-color: transparent;">&nbsp;key in the article body database</span></font></p><p><font style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"><span style="background-color: transparent;">inital_catagories and&nbsp;</span></font><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">claimes</span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));">&nbsp;are added by the summariser MCP server later on</span></p>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="190" width="450" x="850" y="310" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="VjYbdxH-pxDq4qBEVL_5-62" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;overflow=hidden;rounded=0;" value="<h1 style="margin-top: 0px;">Event</h1><p><font style=""><font style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Events are moments or changes that happened today, examples would include are:</font></font></p><p><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">China blocks Meta’s $2bn purchase of AI group Manus.&nbsp;</span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">German energy giant nears £600mn deal to buy UK supplier Ovo.&nbsp;</span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Alleged shooter charged with attempted assassination of Trump at Washington dinner.</span></p><p><font style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"><span style="background-color: transparent;">Events are the primary first level abstraction of news articles. </span><span style="background-color: transparent;"><font style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">O</font></span><font style="background-color: transparent;"><font style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">btained from</font><font style=""> the&nbsp;</font></font><span style="background-color: transparent; white-space: pre;"><font style="">()</font></span><span style="background-color: transparent;">&nbsp;tool in the&nbsp;</span></font><span style="background-color: transparent;">summariser MCP server which o</span><span style="background-color: transparent;">nly computes the event and source_article_ids values.&nbsp;</span></font></p><p><span style="background-color: transparent;">Events now point to articles to enable the analyst MCP server to extract more information in&nbsp;</span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); white-space: pre;"><font face="Consolas, Courier New, monospace">analyse_events</font></span><font style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><span style="font-family: Consolas, &quot;Courier New&quot;, monospace; value="<h1 style="margin-top: 0px;">What does the MCP architecture do exactly?</h1><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p style="text-align: justify;">Each of the 3 MCP servers provide tools to the orchestrator MCP client. This orchestrator has the ability to use any of the tools as and when it chooses however, in our case we give the orchestrator a system prompt telling it to call each tool sequencially forming a dataprocessing pipeline of articles into events, actors and themes before summaring the results.</p><p style="text-align: justify;"><br></p>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="360" width="522.5" x="7.5" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;overflow=hidden;rounded=0;" value="<h1 style="margin-top: 0px;">Collector [@Isaac @Ashley]</h1><p><font face="Courier New">&nbsp;collect_articles() -&gt; list[Article]&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><span style="font-family: &quot;Courier New&quot;; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">(also creates article_db_objects in the database)</span></p><p></p><ul><li>fetches from newsapi and creates <font face="Courier New">article</font>&nbsp;objects from the result based on the top stories from the last 24 hours</li></ul><p></p><p><font face="Courier New">&nbsp;search_news( topics: list[str], start_date: str, end_date: str ) -&gt; list[Article]&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;&nbsp;</font><span style="font-family: &quot;Courier New&quot;; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">(</span><span style="font-family: &quot;Courier New&quot;;">also creates article_db_objects in the database</span><span style="font-family: &quot;Courier New&quot;; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">)</span></p><blockquote style="margin: 0px 0px 0px 40px; border-width: medium; border-style: none; border-color: currentcolor; border-image: initial; padding: 0px;"><li>Currently unused, allows for searching newsapi for more articles about a topic, it creates&nbsp;<font face="Courier New">article</font>&nbsp;objects from the result.<br></li><p></p></blockquote>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="172" width="700" x="40" y="1888" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="VjYbdxH-pxDq4qBEVL_5-105" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;overflow=hidden;rounded=0;" value="<h1 style="margin-top: 0px;">Summariser [@Caleb]</h1><p><span style="font-family: &quot;Courier New&quot;; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">summarise_batch(articles: list[Article]) -&gt; list[Article]</span></p><p></p><ul></ul><p></p><blockquote style="margin: 0px 0px 0px 40px; border-width: medium; border-style: none; border-color: currentcolor; border-image: initial; padding: 0px;"><li>TODO</li></blockquote><p><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-family: &quot;Courier New&quot;;">score_sentiment(articles: list[Article]) -&gt; list[Article]</span></p><ul><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Extracts the claims made by different articles, rate the opinion of a given article on the claims&nbsp;that it makes, and then update the article objects with the newly extracted and processed claims.</span></li></ul><p></p><p><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font face="Courier New">tag_themes(articles: list[Article]) -&gt; list[Article]</font></span></p><p></p><ul></ul><p></p><blockquote style="margin: 0px 0px 0px 40px; border-width: medium; border-style: none; border-color: currentcolor; border-image: initial; padding: 0px;"><li>TODO</li></blockquote><p><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font face="Courier New">extract_act_eve(articles: list[Article]) -&gt; tuple[list[Article], list[Actor], list[Event]]</font></span></p><blockquote style="margin: 0px 0px 0px 40px; border-width: medium; border-style: none; border-color: currentcolor; border-image: initial; padding: 0px;"><li><font face="Helvetica">Extracts the geopolitical actors and events from a list of articles, classifies the actors, and&nbsp;updates the articles with information on the actors and events that they reference. The updated articles, actors and events are then returned.</font></li></blockquote><p><br></p>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="300" width="700" x="40" y="2080" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="VjYbdxH-pxDq4qBEVL_5-106" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;overflow=hidden;rounded=0;" value="<h1 style="margin-top: 0px;">Analyst&nbsp;[@Albert]</h1><p>The analyst server, makes the following tools available:</p><p><font face="Courier New">group_articles(articles: list[Article]) -&gt; dict[str, list[Article]]</font></p><ul><li>TODO</li><ul></ul></ul><p><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font face="Courier New">analyse_events(events: list[Event]) -&gt; list[Event]</font></span></p><p></p><ul><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font face="Helvetica">Populate the events with impact severityies and their justifications in each of the catagorie</font></span></li><ul><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font face="Helvetica">economic impact, finacial markets impact, security impact, diplomatic impact</font></span></li></ul></ul><p></p><p><span style="background-color: transparent;"><font face="Courier New" style="">def gen_report() -&gt; str</font></span></p><p></p><ul><li>This is technically not a tool, its an MCP promt from the analyst MCP server to the orchestrator MCP client instructing it to create the report.</li></ul>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="300" width="710" x="40" y="2380" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="VjYbdxH-pxDq4qBEVL_5-107" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;overflow=hidden;rounded=0;" value="<h1 style="margin-top: 0px;">Orchestrator</h1><p>This is the MCP server in charge. It needs good system prompts with clear instructions about how to use the tools.</p>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="88" width="700" x="40" y="1800" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="VjYbdxH-pxDq4qBEVL_5-108" parent="1" style="swimlane;startSize=0;" value="" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="840" width="550" x="30" y="410" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="VjYbdxH-pxDq4qBEVL_5-109" parent="VjYbdxH-pxDq4qBEVL_5-108" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;overflow=hidden;rounded=0;" value="<h1 style="margin-top: 0px;">Where does all the data go?</h1><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p style="text-align: justify;"><br></p><p style="text-align: justify;"><br></p><p style="text-align: justify;"><br></p><p style="text-align: justify;">Tools implemented under MCP servers are functions that return pydantic objects to the orchestrator MCP server which can provide this data as input to other tools. The exception to this rule is article contents which is stored in an SQLite database by the collector MCP server so as not to overwelm the context window of the llm powering the MCP client.</p><p style="text-align: justify;"><br></p><h1 style="margin-top: 0px;">So what do we have in the end?</h1><div><span style="text-align: justify;">The final thing that the orchestrator will do is to call a tool (technically an mcp prompt not a tool) implemented under the analyst MCP server that will prompt the orchestrator MCP client to form the final report from information in its context window. This context window will include any data that the MCP servers have returned from functions:</span></div><p>A collection of events from the last 24 hours, where each event has listed:</p><p></p><ul><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">The impact on each of our 4 sections including score and justification</span></li><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">The name of any actors involved&nbsp;</span></li><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Relavant theme tags</span></li><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">The source article headlines and metadata sutch as source</span></li></ul><p></p><div>A collection of claims from the last 24 hours with some agreement and variance scores</div><div><br></div><div>A collection of actors from the last 24 hours with analysis of each actor</div><div><br></div><div style="text-align: right;">...as well as many intermediate values which are largely subsets of the above datastructures</div><div style="text-align: right;"><br></div><div><div><span style="text-align: justify;"><br></span></div><div><span style="text-align: justify;">This does <b>not </b>include the article body of the articles as that is never returned from the collector MCP server (so hopefully no direct plagerism is possible).</span></div></div><div><span style="text-align: justify;"><br></span></div><p style="text-align: justify;"><br></p>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="810" width="515" x="15" y="20" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="VjYbdxH-pxDq4qBEVL_5-110" parent="VjYbdxH-pxDq4qBEVL_5-108" span.style: font-family: Consolas, "Courier New", monospace; white-space: pre;

font.span: tool in the collector MCP server. The

span.style: background-color: transparent; font-family: Consolas, "Courier New", monospace; white-space: pre;

font.span: tool can be used to get more articles about a topic.
the article_id is a string of the form: "%publication_date%-%source_id%-%article_title_hash%" it can be used to uniquely identify the article and acts as the
key in the article body database

p.span: claimes
are added by the summariser MCP server later on

p.span: China blocks Meta’s $2bn purchase of AI group Manus.
German energy giant nears £600mn deal to buy UK supplier Ovo.
Alleged shooter charged with attempted assassination of Trump at Washington dinner.

font.span: Events are the primary first level abstraction of news articles.

div.h1: What does the MCP architecture do exactly?
div.p: Each of the 3 MCP servers provide tools to the orchestrator MCP client. This orchestrator has the ability to use any of the tools as and when it chooses however, in our case we give the orchestrator a system prompt telling it to call each tool sequencially forming a dataprocessing pipeline of articles into events, actors and themes before summaring the results.

li.span: Extracts the claims made by different articles, rate the opinion of a given article on the claims that it makes, and then update the article objects with the newly extracted and processed claims.

li.font: Extracts the geopolitical actors and events from a list of articles, classifies the actors, and updates the articles with information on the actors and events that they reference. The updated articles, actors and events are then returned.

span.font: Populate the events with impact severityies and their justifications in each of the catagorie
economic impact, finacial markets impact, security impact, diplomatic impact

ul.li: This is technically not a tool, its an MCP promt from the analyst MCP server to the orchestrator MCP client instructing it to create the report.

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; max-height: 806px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;

div.h1: Where does all the data go?
div.p: Tools implemented under MCP servers are functions that return pydantic objects to the orchestrator MCP server which can provide this data as input to other tools. The exception to this rule is article contents which is stored in an SQLite database by the collector MCP server so as not to overwelm the context window of the llm powering the MCP client.
div.h1: So what do we have in the end?

div.span: The final thing that the orchestrator will do is to call a tool (technically an mcp prompt not a tool) implemented under the analyst MCP server that will prompt the orchestrator MCP client to form the final report from information in its context window. This context window will include any data that the MCP servers have returned from functions:

div.p: A collection of events from the last 24 hours, where each event has listed:

li.span: The impact on each of our 4 sections including score and justification
The name of any actors involved
The source article headlines and metadata sutch as source

div.div: A collection of claims from the last 24 hours with some agreement and variance scores
A collection of actors from the last 24 hours with analysis of each actor

div.style: text-align: right;

div.div: ...as well as many intermediate values which are largely subsets of the above datastructures

div.style: text-align: right;

div.span: This does not include the article body of the articles as that is never returned from the collector MCP server (so hopefully no direct plagerism is possible).
